clips.title: Building verification loops in Claude Code
clips.why: Anthropic's own short video on the idea behind verify: give the agent the checks you would run yourself, so it can tell on its own whether it is done.
look: Hand off your manual checks: everything you would look at before saying done is something the agent can run too.
Codify your checks: write them down as commands, not as advice.
The verification loop: change, check, read the result, change again, until the checks are green.
clips.after: npm run verify and poe verify are those codified checks for fcp, and the Stop hook is what closes the loop for Nova.

clips.title: Claude Code Hooks, Explained Simply.
clips.why: Why a hook beats a sentence in the agent's instructions: the model is probabilistic, a script that runs at a fixed moment is not.
look: Rules in a CLAUDE.md file can be ignored in a long session; a hook always runs.
A hook is just an event plus a script, nothing more magical.
Determinism: the same moment, the same command, every time.
clips.after: That is why fcp does not ask Nova to remember verify: the Stop hook runs it every time Nova wants to stop.

clips.title: Hooks in Claude Code
clips.why: The official tour of hooks: where they are configured, which events exist, and how a team shares them.
look: The lifecycle events, and that Stop is the moment the agent wants to finish.
Hooks in the project's settings file are shared with everyone who opens the repo.
A hook can block an action and tell Claude why.
clips.after: fcp's hook lives in the committed .claude/settings.json, so engineers and Nova, which loads the same project settings, get the same check.

practice.q: On the ticket's branch, the only change since main is a new file docs/empty-state.md. Which steps does npm run verify run?

options.text: Lint, types and the related unit tests
options.why: verify only looks at .ts, .tsx, .css and .json files, so a Markdown file is not handed to Biome or Vitest.
No code file changed, so there is nothing to lint and no test imports the file. The type check runs every time anyway.

options.text: Nothing at all, and it exits with 0
options.why: The type check is never skipped, so even a docs-only change gets one step.

practice.q: Finish the Stop hook's failure branch so Claude Code does not let the agent stop, and shows it the summary.
practice.hint: The one exit code that blocks a stop.
practice.why: Exit 2 blocks the stop and hands stderr to the agent as its next message. Exit 1 is a non-blocking error: the agent stops anyway.

practice.q: Complete the Vitest command that runs every test importing the changed files.
practice.hint: One word: the tests that are ... to these files.
practice.why: vitest related follows the import graph from the given source files to every test that uses them.

practice.q: frontend-ci keeps its own lint, check-types and unit test steps, and people use npm run verify locally. What is the risk?

options.why: Speed is about the same. The risk is about meaning, not time.

options.text: The two lists drift apart, so green on a laptop no longer means green on the PR.
options.why: Someone adds a check to one and not the other. When CI runs npm run verify -- --all, there is only one list.

options.text: Biome runs twice and the results disagree.
options.why: The same tool on the same files gives the same result. The problem is two separate lists of steps.

practice.q: Put what happens in order when Nova says done while the type check is red.
items: Nova wants to end its turn, so Claude Code runs the Stop hook
The hook runs npm run verify, which prints FAIL types and exits with 1
The hook writes the summary to stderr and exits with 2
Nova gets the summary as its next message and fixes the projects page
Nova stops again, verify is green, and the hook exits with 0
practice.why: The hook does not fix anything itself. It only turns a red verify into one more round of work, and lets the agent go when the answer is green.

practice.q: A new laptop runs poe verify and every backend step fails with "No interpreter found for Python 3.13". Which command answers what is wrong?

options.why: That checks the code. The problem is the machine, so a bigger code check fails the same way.
doctor checks the machine against what fcp needs and prints FIX with the command to run, here uv python install 3.13.
That is the frontend's verify. It does not look at the Python setup.
